source: Related work. Linear probing at least traces back to Hewitt and Manning [15], who examines the correlation between BERT’s hidden states and the parse tree distance metric (similar to NTdistance in our language). Subsequent studies [8, 18, 20, 30, 34, 36, 40] also explored probing techniques to suggest that BERT-like transformers can approximate CFGs from natural languages. Our approach differs not only in the multi-head probing formula that we proposed; also that we use synthetic data to demonstrate that linear probing can almost perfectly recover NT ancestors and boundaries, even for complex and ambiguous CFG strings exceeding hundreds of tokens.
